history.summary: Khajrana Ganesh Temple, in the Khajrana area of Indore, was built in 1735 by Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar of the Holkar dynasty. The Ganesha idol, said to have been hidden in a well to protect it during Aurangzeb's campaigns, was reportedly revealed in a dream to local priest Pandit Mangal Bhatt; it was retrieved from the well and enshrined here, and the Bhatt family has managed the temple ever since. From a small hut it has grown into a large complex with a silver-plated garbhagriha gate and walls, diamond-set eyes on the deity, and 33 smaller shrines. It is one of India's richest temples through devotee donations, is under the control of the District Magistrate of Indore, and is famous for the custom of devotees drawing an inverted swastika behind the idol while making a wish.

town_description: Indore is the largest city and commercial capital of Madhya Pradesh, and was the capital of the Holkar dynasty under the Marathas. It blends historic landmarks like Rajwada palace and Lal Bagh Palace with a renowned food culture centred on Sarafa Bazaar. It has repeatedly been ranked India's cleanest city and is a major hub for education, trade, and tourism in central India.
